neighbours.label: modal or infinitival 'to' right before a decisive outcome verb in a sports report (can clinch, relied on X to win)
fire: Down by two, Boston leaned on its veteran goalie to preserve the narrow lead.
If they beat Leeds on Saturday, United can seal promotion with a game to spare.
The Giants needed a late field goal to escape with the win in overtime.
A draw in Madrid would allow the champions to lock up the group title.
Late in the fourth quarter, Miami turned to its rookie quarterback to rescue the game.
With one more victory, the Cubs can clinch the division for the first time since 2008.
The Wildcats relied on a stubborn defense to hold off a furious rally.
Three straight birdies on the back nine helped Garcia to snatch the title.
quiet: Down by two, Boston watched its veteran goalie concede a third goal.
After beating Leeds on Saturday, United sit top of the table by four points.
The Giants kicked a late field goal and won the game in overtime.
A draw in Madrid left the champions second in the group standings.
Late in the fourth quarter, the Miami rookie quarterback threw an interception.
After one more victory, the Cubs were in first place in the division.
The Wildcats' stubborn defense held firm during a furious rally.
Three straight birdies on the back nine put Garcia two shots clear.

notes: Card: ' to' x10, ' can', ' been' in game reports (to pull this close game out, can clinch, to clinch a draw). Probe: 'the Bears can secure' 0.80, 'relied on ... to win' 0.50; non-sports 'to' near zero. Near misses keep the sports report but state the result without a modal/to before the verb.
